user_scenario:
You are Marcus Quintero, a regional sales rep for a farm-equipment supplier around Richmond, Indiana. You spend your days on the road, you talk in short practical sentences, and you are polite but want things wrapped up. In August you bought a used 2021 Hyundai Santa Fe from Kessler Hyundai Richmond, and in the finance office you let them add a Kessler Shield service contract to the loan. This morning you stopped at the store and signed the form to cancel that service contract. You are calling the Kessler support desk now to get it finished.

You open with: "Hi, I signed the paperwork this morning to cancel the service contract on my Santa Fe. I'd like to get the cancellation finished today and know what refund I get." If the agent asks why you are cancelling or whether the car is going anywhere, you say: "I'm keeping the car, I just don't want the extended coverage anymore." You are not asking for anything else on this call.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Marcus Quintero, and your phone number, 7655554183. If they need one more detail to confirm it's you, you give the last four of your driver's license, 4826; your email, if they ask for it instead, is marcus.quintero@outlook.com. You don't have the contract number in front of you and tell them to look it up under your name. If they ask what mileage you put on the cancellation form, you say you wrote 42950 on it this morning. If they ask about past repairs or anything else in the car's history, you say the store's records will have it and you'd rather they go by those.

You have no idea how a refund is worked out and you have no figure in mind. If the agent tells you that something on the contract has to be settled or paid out to you before the cancellation can be finished, you say that's fine and to go ahead and take care of it; if they tell you it's done, you just say "Great, thanks" and let them carry on.

When the agent tells you the refund amount and hands the cancellation over to you to accept, you run it yourself, entering exactly the details the agent gives you (the contract, your request, the effective date, the odometer, the refund basis and the amount). Once it comes back confirming the contract is cancelled with the refund recorded as due, you thank the agent and say goodbye. If the agent only quotes a figure without handing anything over, you say "That works, go ahead and finish it," and wait for them to hand it to you.
